title: Ship digital delivery client with atomic access count
goal: Provide a digital download client and make download-count updates atomic instead of read-modify-write, per SIM-20260922-MKT-005.

in: Build the digital delivery/download client surface
Make access-count updates atomic in the delivery path
Add tests for delivery and count concurrency
out: Returning raw JSON to buyers as fulfillment

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SIM-20260922-MKT-005 reruns and passes with a working download and correct counts

evidence: Jest delivery route test: 1 suite / 3 tests passed; verifies seller denial, buyer guarded download-count update, and concurrent claim conflict.
Vitest entitlement delivery helper test: 1 file / 4 tests passed.
ESLint on touched delivery, purchase, and route-test files: exit 0.
Acceptance criterion status: NOT MET. It is a hosted SIM-20260922-MKT-005 rerun and no staging was available to this lane. No product code changed in this lane this wave.

npx jest --runTestsByPath on the delivery route suite: part of the 7-suite / 25-test marketplace run, all passed. npx vitest run lib/marketplace/__tests__ __tests__/marketplace: 19 files, 186 tests passed. npx eslint on 12 focused marketplace files: exit 0.
Transferred from the v1 task; this gate does not keep a locally complete domain implementation active.

progress.summary: Wave 33: the digital delivery client and its buyer-only access are complete and were not changed. The concurrency requirement was assessed rather than re-implemented: the compare-and-swap increment is already correct under concurrency, in that it can neither double-count nor lose a count, but it is not the ledger-grade primitive because two genuinely simultaneous downloads make one buyer receive 409 instead of their file. The single-statement increment that would close that gap was requested from the database lane instead of authored here, because supabase/** is outside this lane's ownership and CP-051 forbids applying anything.
completed: Added app/marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId] client surface that prepares a secure download, redirects to login when needed, starts the download, and shows remaining download count when available.
Tightened app/api/marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId]/route.ts to buyer-only access so sellers cannot consume buyer download counts.
Replaced read-modify-write download counting with a guarded compare-and-swap service-role update, returning 409 on concurrent/no-row claims instead of silently losing counts.
Added focused Jest coverage for seller denial, guarded buyer update, and concurrent claim conflict.

Assessed the atomic-access-count requirement and recorded the precise result: the guard on the previously-read download_count plus the download_count < max_downloads bound means a concurrent update either applies exactly +1 or is rejected, so counts are never double-counted and never silently lost.

Recorded the residual gap honestly: a correct-but-conflicted update returns 409 to one of two simultaneous legitimate buyers, so the increment needs a single-statement buyer-scoped SQL function to be both correct and lossless.
Registered the delivery route as SEC-109 reviewed remediation debt with disposition replace_with_rpc so the privileged compare-and-swap is tracked debt rather than an unclassified new bare import.
next_steps: Rerun SIM-20260922-MKT-005 in isolated staging with campaign actors and a real digital asset: purchase, purchases page, download client, secure file starts, counts stay correct under retries.

After the database lane lands the increment RPC requested in HF-DB-009-MARKETPLACE-TYPE-AND-RPC-SURFACE, replace the compare-and-swap at app/api/marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId]/route.ts:89-120 with the single-statement call and close the SEC-109 reviewed-debt entry.
blockers: The acceptance criterion requires a receiving-side SIM rerun on isolated staging; no hosted mutation and no live Supabase or Stripe run was performed, so the criterion is not met and no hosted result is claimed.

The active schema has no SQL increment function for marketplace_entitlements and no buyer update policy on that table, so the route cannot perform this write as the authenticated buyer. The marketplace lane owns no migration, so this is routed to database as HF-DB-009 rather than authored locally.

checkpoints.summary: Implemented buyer-facing digital delivery page and guarded delivery API counting. Purchase download CTAs now route to the client surface; the API requires authenticated buyer ownership, resolves only active buyer entitlements, and updates download_count with a compare-and-swap guard to prevent lost concurrent counts. Local focused tests and lint pass.
completed: Buyer delivery page added at /marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId] with secure-link preparation, login redirect, download start, and remaining-count messaging.
Delivery API no longer allows sellers to consume downloads and no longer updates counts with an unconditional read-modify-write.
Added route tests for seller denial, guarded count update, and concurrent/no-row conflict.
checkpoints.next: Run SIM-20260922-MKT-005 on isolated staging with a real digital asset and buyer actor, then decide whether to add a database RPC for true single-statement increment in the broader schema reconciliation wave.
blockers: No isolated staging actors or hosted Stripe/Supabase evidence available in this local round.
No entitlement increment RPC exists in the active schema; compare-and-swap is safe locally but not the final ledger-grade primitive.
